definitions.explanation: A large, very sweet citrus variety identified by a distinctive bump (デコ) at the top. A hybrid of ponkan and a Kiyomi orange, mostly grown in Kumamoto and Ehime.

examples.english: Dekopons have a bump on top.

examples.japanese: デコポン⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧みかん⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{大|おお}きくて→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦{甘|あま}い→甘い：00617_amai⟧。
examples.english: Dekopons are bigger and sweeter than regular mandarins.

examples.japanese: {熊本|くまもと}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{全国|ぜんこく}→全国：03311_zenkoku⟧⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧デコポン⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{産地|さんち}→産地：04031_sanchi⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: Kumamoto is known as the top dekopon-producing region in Japan.

notes:
The name combines デコ (bump) + ポン (from ⟦ポンカン→ポンカン：28932_ponkan⟧, one of the parent varieties). Officially the variety is {不知火|しらぬい}; デコポン is a registered brand name for the highest-grade fruit. In daily speech, almost everyone uses デコポン regardless of grade.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- デコポン⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{皮|かわ}→皮：02187_kawa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{剥|む}く→剥く：02305_muku⟧: to peel a dekopon
- {熊本|くまもと}{産|さん}デコポン: Kumamoto-grown dekopon

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不知火|しらぬい}: shiranui — the official variety name; same fruit, non-brand
- ⟦{温州|うんしゅう}みかん→温州みかん：28931_unshuumikan⟧: satsuma mandarin — much smaller, milder, no top bump
